name: Channel Mapparr
description: Standardizes broadcast (OTA) and premium/cable channel names using network data and channel lists. Supports M3U stream import, category organization, and fuzzy matching across 42K+ channels in 11 countries.
author: PiratesIRC

fields.label: Matching and Scope
fields.description: Which channel databases a run matches against, how close a name has to be before it counts as a match, and which channel groups are in scope. The two group settings are not opposites: Channel Groups to Process narrows a run to the groups you name, while Channel Groups to Ignore is a refusal that every action obeys, including the ones that only replay a saved results file. A name in Channel Groups to Ignore that matches no group refuses most actions rather than being skipped, because a typo there would otherwise quietly widen the run to everything. The actions that replay a saved results file cannot refuse, because they never ask the database which groups exist; they filter on the group name stored in that file.

fields.label: Channel Databases
fields.help_text: Comma-separated country codes deciding which channel databases are loaded. Available: AU, BR, CA, DE, ES, FR, IN, MX, NL, NO, PL, UK, US. The same codes choose which tv-logos directories the per-channel logo action searches, so a country left out here is left out of both.

fields.label: Match Sensitivity

options.label: Relaxed (70 of 100), more matches and more mistakes
Strict (90 of 100), fewer matches and higher confidence

fields.help_text: How close a name has to be before it counts as a match, scored out of 100. A lower threshold finds more matches and makes more mistakes. The threshold each choice uses is recorded at the top of every CSV export.

fields.label: Channel Groups to Process
fields.help_text: Comma-separated channel group names. Limits renaming, tagging and logo actions to these groups. Leave empty to process every group. This setting includes; Channel Groups to Ignore excludes, and an exclusion wins.

fields.label: Channel Groups to Ignore
fields.help_text: Comma-separated. Channels in these groups are excluded from renaming, tagging, logos and Organize by Category, regardless of 'Channel Groups to Process' or 'Category Organization Groups'. Supports * and ? wildcards; matching is case-insensitive. An entry that matches no channel group refuses most actions. Organize by Category skips an ignored target group and continues. Import M3U Streams does not check entries against every group; it only refuses if its own target group is ignored.

fields.label: Category Organization Groups
fields.help_text: Comma-separated group names that Organize by Category is allowed to move channels into or create. Leave empty to use the categories named in the channel database files. A group listed in Channel Groups to Ignore is skipped and the run continues.

fields.label: Import M3U Streams
fields.description: The four settings Import M3U Streams uses to decide which provider streams to bring in and where to put them. That action creates one channel per STREAM, so a provider serving the same station once per M3U account produces one channel per account rather than one channel with several streams attached. Create Channels From Streams, in the next section, is the one that makes a single channel per station.

fields.label: M3U Source
fields.help_text: Which M3U account the import reads streams from. All sources reads every one. The list is built from Dispatcharr M3U Accounts when the settings page loads, so an account added since you opened this page will not appear until you reload it.

fields.label: M3U Group Filter
fields.help_text: Comma-separated M3U group titles to import from. This filter is applied BEFORE matching, so a stream in a group not listed here is never looked at. Leave empty to read every group.

fields.label: Category Filter
fields.help_text: Comma-separated category names from the channel database. This filter is applied AFTER matching, so a stream is matched first and then kept only if its category is listed. Leave empty to keep every category.

fields.label: Custom Import Group Name
fields.help_text: Put every imported channel in this one group instead of sorting them into groups by category. Leave empty to name the groups after the category each channel matched.

fields.label: Create Channels From Streams
fields.description: The settings for the action that creates one channel per broadcast station, for streams no channel is using yet. It attaches no streams: it creates the channels and stops, leaving the stream assignment to another tool or to hand. Networks to Skip reads what a station IS rather than every network its record mentions, so a CBS station carrying a second network on a subchannel is still treated as a CBS station and is not skipped.

fields.label: Stream Groups to Seed From
fields.help_text: Used by Create Channels From Streams. Comma-separated names of the stream groups to scan. Only streams in these groups that are not attached to any channel are considered. Leave empty to do nothing.

fields.label: Channel Group to Create In
fields.help_text: Used by Create Channels From Streams. The existing channel group the new channels are created in. The group must already exist. A group listed in Channel Groups to Ignore is refused.

fields.label: First Channel Number to Use
fields.help_text: Used by Create Channels From Streams. The first channel number to assign. Numbers already in use are skipped, so the run does not need a free block. Leave empty to start above the highest channel number on the system.

fields.label: Networks to Skip When Creating Channels
fields.help_text: Used by Create Channels From Streams. Comma-separated network names. A station carrying one of them is reported and skipped rather than created. The network is read from the station record and from the stream name, because a low power record often names no network at all. Leave empty to create every station that matches.

fields.label: Names, Tags and Logos
fields.description: How a matched channel is named, what marks one that did not match, and which logo it gets. Match by Market When No Callsign is off by default and changes nothing for a channel whose name already prints a callsign; it only affects names that state a market and a channel number instead, and it accepts a station only when exactly one fits. Ignored Tags are stripped before matching rather than from the channel name itself.

fields.label: OTA Name Format
fields.help_text: Template for the name given to a matched broadcast channel. The placeholders are {NETWORK}, {STATE}, {CITY} and {CALLSIGN}, and the default produces a name such as ABC - NY New York (WABC-TV). A channel whose station record is missing one of the placeholders you use is left alone rather than renamed with a gap.

fields.label: Match by Market When No Callsign
fields.help_text: When a name states a market and a channel number but no callsign, such as ABC 9 HD [SYRACUSE], look the station up by market instead. A station is accepted only when exactly one fits, so an ambiguous market is left alone. Leave this off to match on callsigns only.

fields.label: Unknown Channel Suffix
fields.help_text: Text appended by Tag Unknown Channels to a channel the matcher could not identify. Include the leading space if you want one, as the default does. Leave empty to tag nothing.

fields.label: Ignored Tags
fields.help_text: Comma-separated tags removed from a name before it is matched, which leaves the channel name itself untouched. Write a tag in brackets or parentheses, such as [HD] or (PRIME), to match it literally; a bare word is matched on word boundaries.

fields.label: Default Logo
fields.help_text: The display name of a logo on the Dispatcharr Logos page, matched without regard to case. Apply Default Logo gives it to every channel in scope that has no logo yet. For a different logo per channel, use Apply Per-Channel Logos instead. Leave empty to skip.

fields.label: Run Behaviour and Housekeeping
fields.description: Settings that apply to any action rather than to one of them: whether a run only previews its changes, how hard it works the database while it runs, and how long its CSV exports are kept. Dry Run Mode is what produces the preview CSV files; with it off the same actions write to your channels. Old exports are deleted only at the moment a new one is written, so nothing is removed on a day you do not run the plugin.

fields.label: Dry Run Mode
fields.help_text: With this on, no action writes to the database. Rename Channels, Organize by Category, Import M3U Streams and Create Channels From Streams write a CSV preview to /data/exports. Tag Unknown Channels, Apply Default Logo and Apply Per-Channel Logos (tv-logos) report a count of what they would have done and write no file. Worth turning on the first time you run any of them with new settings.

fields.label: Rate Limiting
fields.help_text: How long to pause between database writes during a large import, to leave Dispatcharr responsive while one runs. It makes a run slower and changes nothing about the result.

fields.label: Delete CSV Exports Older Than (Days)
fields.help_text: Housekeeping for the CSV files this plugin writes to /data/exports. After each export, this plugin's own exports older than this many days are deleted. 0 keeps every file, which is the default, so nothing is removed unless you ask for it. The file just written is never deleted, and at least one file always survives. Only files named channel_mapparr_*.csv are touched, because that directory is shared with other plugins. Clear CSV Exports still deletes all of them regardless of this setting.

fields.label: Emailed Reports
fields.description: Whether this plugin hands a report to the Newsflasharr plugin, after which runs, and in which format. Nothing is sent unless Newsflasharr is installed and carries a routing rule matching this plugin and its usage report event; without that rule the report is delivered as plain text with no attachment, because attachments are email only. This plugin has no scheduler, so a report is only ever produced by a run you start yourself.

fields.label: Send notifications to Newsflasharr
fields.help_text: Requires the Newsflasharr plugin, which is what actually sends the mail. What routes where is configured in Newsflasharr's routing rules, keyed on this plugin's name. Channel Mapparr does not require Newsflasharr to be installed: with it absent or disabled, nothing is sent and nothing fails.

fields.label: Email A Report After

options.label: Every run that produces an export

fields.help_text: Which runs email a report. The emailed report is built specifically for sending: it never contains your M3U source names, which the CSV exports in /data/exports do contain in their settings header. Organize by Category reports only in Dry Run, because a real run of it produces no export. This setting does nothing unless Send notifications to Newsflasharr is on above.

fields.label: Email Report Format

options.label: Both, which arrives as two emails

fields.help_text: Which report file to email. A notification carries one attachment, so choosing both sends two separate emails per run rather than one email with two files. The HTML page is easier to read and the CSV is easier to sort and filter. Both files are written to /data/channel_mapparr_reports either way; this setting only decides which are emailed.

fields.label: Anonymous Usage Counts
fields.description: The setting below sends this plugin's Channels Renamed total and a random id to the plugin author's counter so the public badges can count installs. No channel names, group names, providers or settings are sent. Untick it to stop; the README section Anonymous usage counts has the details.

fields.label: Share anonymous usage counts
fields.help_text: Sends this plugin's Channels Renamed total and a random id for this plugin on this install to the plugin author's counter at plugin-stats.dpas.workers.dev when the plugin runs, at most once an hour, or ten minutes after the last report when the plugin has just recorded new work, so the README badges count every install that runs at least one action. The server stores that id with the total and the date of the last report. The connection shows the server your public IP address; the server uses it only to limit abuse and does not store it in its database, though when an install first registers it keeps a salted one-way hash of it (of its /64 block for IPv6) for up to three days. Cloudflare, which hosts the server, keeps its own request logs. No names, channels, streams, providers or settings are sent. Untick to stop sending; this install's figures are deleted from the server the next time the plugin runs after you untick.

actions.label: Validate Settings
actions.description: Check database connectivity, channel databases, and settings before running any action.

actions.label: Load & Process Channels
actions.description: Scan channel groups and determine standardized names.

actions.label: Rename Channels
actions.description: Apply standardized names to processed channels. Dry Run exports a CSV preview instead.

confirm.message: This will rename channels to the standardized format. This action is irreversible. Continue?

actions.label: Tag Unknown Channels
actions.description: Append the configured suffix to unmatched OTA and premium channels.

confirm.message: This will append the configured suffix to unmatched channels. Continue?

actions.label: Apply Default Logo
actions.description: Assign the configured default logo to channels that don't have one.

confirm.message: This will apply the default logo to channels without a logo. Continue?

actions.label: Apply Per-Channel Logos (tv-logos)
actions.description: Fuzzy-match each channel name to the tv-logo/tv-logos GitHub repo and assign per-channel logos. Uses the country codes from Channel Databases. Channels with an existing logo are left alone.

confirm.message: This will fetch tv-logos and assign per-channel logos to channels without one. Continue?

actions.label: Organize by Category
actions.description: Move channels into category-based groups. Runs in the web request, so a large run can take a while before the page answers. Dry Run exports a CSV preview.

confirm.message: This will create new groups (if needed) and move channels to category-based groups. Continue?

actions.label: Import M3U Streams
actions.description: Create channels from M3U streams organized by category. Runs in background. Dry Run exports a CSV preview.

confirm.message: This will create new channels from M3U streams and organize them into groups. Duplicates get suffixes. Continue?

actions.label: Create Channels From Streams
actions.description: Create one channel per broadcast station for streams that are not attached to any channel yet. Unlike Import M3U Streams this creates one channel per station rather than one per stream, and it attaches no streams. Runs in background. Dry Run exports a CSV preview.

confirm.message: This will create new channels in the target group. No streams are attached. Continue?

actions.label: Show Status
actions.description: Show live progress and ETA for the most recent or running operation. Reads a persistent progress file so you can check without watching container logs.

actions.label: Email Report Now
actions.description: Build a report from the last processed channels and queue it for email. Requires the Newsflasharr plugin installed and enabled, its email settings configured, and a routing rule sending this plugin to email. This button checks all of that first and refuses rather than queueing a report nobody receives. It changes nothing. Queued means written to Newsflasharr's queue, not yet in your inbox. It does NOT prove the automatic path works, because it runs here in the web worker using the settings currently on screen.

actions.label: Clear CSV Exports
actions.description: Delete all CSV export files created by this plugin.

confirm.message: Delete all Channel Mapparr CSV exports?
